table_title: List the well-documented extinct animal taxa — species, subspecies, and regional populations — whose last confirmed individual was recorded in 1900 or later per Wikipedia's 'List of recently extinct mammals', 'List of bird extinctions by year', and the per-taxon Wikipedia articles, with each taxon's common name, scientific name, continent of origin, year of last confirmed record (wild or captive, whichever later, per the per-taxon article), and the primary cause(s) of extinction.
db_analog: SELECT t.common_name, t.scientific_name, t.continent_of_origin, t.year_of_last_confirmed_record, GROUP_CONCAT(c.cause, '; ') AS primary_causes FROM extinct_taxa t JOIN taxon_causes c ON c.taxon_id = t.id WHERE t.year_of_last_confirmed_record_numeric >= 1900 AND t.documentation_quality = 'well_documented' AND t.scope IN ('species', 'subspecies', 'regional_population') GROUP BY t.id ORDER BY t.year_of_last_confirmed_record_numeric ASC, t.common_name ASC
temporal_note: Wikipedia 'List of recently extinct mammals' + 'List of bird extinctions by year' master articles + 22 per-taxon Wikipedia articles (one per staged taxon), all accessed 2026-05-11. The universe is 22 well-documented extinct animal taxa (12 full species + 6 subspecies + 4 regional/local-form populations) whose last confirmed record is 1900 or later per the per-taxon Wikipedia article. Year of Last Confirmed Record captures the latest verified record per the per-taxon article — wild sighting, captive individual, or specimen collection, whichever is most recent. Most rows resolve to a specific 4-digit year (21 of 22); Bali tiger uses the article's stated form 'late 1930s' because the article gives no single year for the last record. Continent of Origin: 6-continent classification with continental-affinity rule for islands (Caribbean→North America, Hawaii/Pacific→Oceania, Tasmania→Oceania, Madagascar→Africa). Primary Causes: semicolon-delimited list per cited per-taxon article (Boundary-Aware Fields pattern). All facts are stable historical record. Cycle-2 audit fix (3 BLOCKING + 2 HYG): (B1) Year relation pivot 'declared extinct' → 'last confirmed sighting' (wild or captive, whichever later) per per-taxon Wikipedia articles — Caspian tiger '1970s' → 1970, Javan tiger '1980s' → 1976, Bali tiger '1950s' → 'late 1930s', etc.; (B2) all 22 cause cells re-grounded against per-taxon Wikipedia articles — Caribbean monk seal 'Hunting; Habitat loss' → 'Overhunting; Overfishing', Japanese wolf 'Hunting' → 'Disease; Persecution; Habitat loss', Heath hen 'Habitat destruction' → 'Hunting; Habitat loss; Inbreeding; Disease', etc.; (B3) row universe reframed as taxa+populations (4 tiger/lion rows are regional populations of broader subspecies per current Wikipedia taxonomy — Bali/Caspian/Javan tigers under P. t. sondaica or P. t. tigris; Barbary lion under P. l. leo); (H1) cycle-0 active-state narrative residue scrubbed from collection_summary, decision_log, open_questions; (H2) source_coverage_notes tightened to honestly attribute Continent + Causes grounding to per-taxon articles, not master articles. Cycle-3 audit fix (1 BLOCKING + 1 HYG): (B1) Barbary lion 1942 → 1956 (article documents later Algerian sighting); Wake Island rail 1945 → 1939 (1945 was WWII-window endpoint, not a verified individual record — 1939 last museum specimen is the authoritative verified record under our rule). (H1) Multi-cause/single-cause narrative count corrected 19/3 → 21/1 (only Bubal hartebeest stays single-cause).
_extraction_notes: Causal instance: cause-effect relation between taxon extinction and primary cause(s). Universe = 22 well-documented animal taxa whose last confirmed record is 1900 or later per the per-taxon Wikipedia article: 12 full species + 6 subspecies + 4 regional/local-form populations (cycle-2 audit fix B3: 'taxa+populations' framing). Taxa breakdown: SPECIES (12) = Passenger pigeon, Carolina parakeet, Hawaiian ʻōʻō, Thylacine, Toolache wallaby, Laysan rail, Wake Island rail, Caribbean monk seal, Japanese sea lion, Atitlán grebe, Poʻouli, Bramble Cay melomys. SUBSPECIES (6) = Japanese wolf (Canis lupus hodophilax), Tarpan (Equus ferus ferus), Bubal hartebeest (Alcelaphus buselaphus buselaphus), Heath hen (Tympanuchus cupido cupido), Pyrenean ibex (Capra pyrenaica pyrenaica), Western black rhinoceros (Diceros bicornis longipes). REGIONAL POPULATIONS (4, formerly classified as subspecies but current Wikipedia taxonomy treats as populations of broader subspecies) = Bali tiger (Bali population of P. t. sondaica), Javan tiger (Java population of P. t. sondaica), Caspian tiger (population of P. t. tigris), Barbary lion (North African population of P. l. leo). Schema: 5 cols (Common Name PK + Scientific Name + Continent + Year of Last Confirmed Record [TEXT, source-exact] + Primary Causes [TEXT, semicolon-delimited]). 21 of 22 rows are multi-cause (semicolon-delimited); 1 is single-cause (Bubal hartebeest 'Overhunting' — article frames as sole cause). Year-form: 21 specific-year rows + 1 decade-only row (Bali tiger 'late 1930s' — article gives no single year). Causes vocabulary (cycle-2 audit re-grounded — 13 distinct values per per-taxon articles): Hunting, Overhunting, Poaching, Overfishing, Habitat loss, Disease, Invasive species, Climate change, Persecution, Prey decline, Inbreeding, Competition, Hybridization. Continent of Origin: 5 distinct (Africa 3, Asia 5, Europe 2, North America 5, Oceania 7). Sort order: Year (parsed-numeric for sort; 'late 1930s' sorts as 1937) ASC, Common Name ASC. Cycles 1+2+3 + Fields-Medal-cycles + painters-cycle + cycle-2-extinctions lessons applied: (a) single PK on Common Name; (b) per-row Wikipedia citation via 2 master articles + 22 per-taxon articles; (c) Year filter '≥ 1900 strict on last confirmed record'; (d) Boundary-Aware Fields pattern for multi-cause Primary Causes; (e) explicit rule for wild-or-captive last record; (f) honest scope framing taxa+populations. Cycle-2 audit fix (3 BLOCKING + 2 HYG) — see curation.json audit_response.cycle_2 for full per-fix details.
